    - heading "Meet your Meta Account" [level=2]
    - paragraph: The simple and easy way to log in and manage your favorite apps.
    - text: No need to juggle multiple logins – with a Meta Account, you can securely sign in and manage whichever profiles you choose.
    - group "Video player"
    - button "Play video"
    - heading "More secure and convenient" [level=2]
    - text: One key, stronger lock With your Meta Account, you can use a single passkey across your Meta apps and devices. A passkey is easier and more secure than traditional passwords. Just log in using your fingerprint, face recognition or device password, all of which are stored on your device and never shared with Meta. WhatsApp passkeys are managed separately.
    - link "Learn more about passkeys and single sign-on":

      - text: Learn more

    - list:
      - listitem:
        - heading "Up-to-date security" [level=3]
        - region: Your Meta Account helps keep your account protections strong and up-to-date. When you use Security Checkup, it recommends actions you can take to strengthen your account, including setting up two-factor authentication, login alerts and more.
    - heading "More convenient controls" [level=2]
    - text: Manage multiple profiles With your Meta Account, you get more flexibility and control. You can manage more key settings in one place and tailor your social experience for each app you choose to include.

limitations: Event sequence records provider receipt order; simultaneous browser causality is not inferred.
Network content is retained only when selected; Playwright response-body bytes are API results and are not guaranteed to match wire bytes.
Request bytes are limited to what Playwright exposes; not_exposed does not establish body absence or multipart file coverage.
Network content reads settle within 5 seconds each and the observer does not request bodies from unfinished responses.
Playwright scenario events do not expose request initiator stacks; receipt order does not prove causality.
Storage values are hashed only after declared-secret redaction.
